newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks fall 1.28 percent by lunch break.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks fall 1.28 percent by lunch break.

text.p: Investor jitters over the Thai baht's continuing slide against the greenback on Monday drove the stock market down 1.28 percent in thin turnover by the lunch break, brokers said.

"Investors are a bit worried about the fall in the baht and reports about an intervention by the Bank of Thailand to prevent the currency from falling further. This has led them to sell large capitalised stocks," said Bunsom Kesapradist of Asia Credit.
The composite SET index was down 8.05 points at 620.50 on 1.7 billion baht turnover at the break.

Dealers said the Bank of Thailand intervened in the domestic market on Monday morning and sold dollars at the 30.75-30.80 per dollar level to try to prevent the baht from falling further against the U.S. unit

The baht was quoted at a new record low of around 30.30/30.75 per dollar early onshore compared with 30.00/30.60 late on Friday. The baht dived on commercial selling for dollars and on hangover from the Philippine peso slide.
Most of the bourse's key sectors fell by the break. The banking sector, which dipped 0.55 percent, was first-ranked in terms of value.
Industrial project owner Bangpakong Industrial Park 2 Plc, which made its debut on Monday, was at 12.75 baht by the break, down from its initial public offer price of 18 baht.
Bangkok Bank gained three baht to 165 and Nava Finance and Securities shed 0.25 to 18.50.
